title: reading-notes-llm-deployment-clara-nguyen
content:
Quick summary / purpose:
- Personal reading notes focused on deployment patterns for LLMs: runtime optimizations, quantization tradeoffs, caching strategies, fallback routing, and production failure modes.
- Mix of paper summaries, blog links, conference takeaways, and small experiment ideas to try on Redwood Dedicated.

Papers & highlights (short bullets):
- "Optimizing Transformer Inference" (example paper) — key takeaways:
  * KV cache management matters a lot for multi-turn chat; flush policies + incremental checkpoints can save recompute for long sessions.
  * Continuous batching heuristics: mix latency-sensitive single-user requests with background batch jobs using priority windows.
- "Post-Training Quantization for LLMs" (arXiv 2023) — practical notes:
  * 4-bit quant often works for encoder-decoder models with calibration; watch out for attention softmax instability.
  * Calibration dataset should match prompt distribution (prefix-heavy apps need longer calibration sequences).
- "Adaptive Model Routing" (systems paper) — notes:
  * Routing by latency SLO + cost preference can route to quantized variant or smaller family model.
  * Need metrics: token-level latency, quality delta, and switch oscillation detection (avoid flapping).

Blog posts & threads to revisit:
- "How to Serve Open LLMs in Production" (company blog) — checklist items we should integrate into onboarding template: metrics, warmup, KV cache priming, and cold-start mitigation.
- Twitter thread on prompt prefix caching — simple trick: hash prefix and maintain LRU cache for encoded prefixes; safe memory bounds with size-based eviction.

Conference takeaways (ICLR 2025 notes):
- Session on "Latency-aware architectures": several demos of attention approximations that shave 10-30% wall-clock but increase implementation complexity. Worth prototyping with kernel fusion.
- Poster on per-request dynamic batching: minimal code changes required on runtime side; scheduler adjustments + backpressure signals did most of the work.

Experiments to run (prioritized):
1) Quantization sweep: run 8-bit, 6-bit, 4-bit PTQ on 3 representative models (chat, summarization, reranker). Metrics: perplexity drift, end-to-end latency (p95), and memory footprint. Use Redwood Dedicated GPU pool with isolated runs.
2) KV cache eviction policy ablation: LRU vs size-aware vs time-based TTL on multi-turn chat workload. Look at token re-generation rates and p95 latency.
3) Prefix caching micro-experiment: implement hash-based prefix encoder cache in the inference shim. Measure cache hit ratio and token-level savings.
4) Fallback routing simulation: inject capacity failure and test automated fallback to quantized model variant; monitor quality regressions with a small eval set and alert thresholds.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How aggressive can we be with PTQ before customer-visible regressions for instruction-following models? Need human eval on a small suite.
- For live traffic, what's the acceptable oscillation rate for routing decisions (how quickly can we switch models before users notice)?
- Are there simple kernel fusion wins we can land without deep custom CUDA work? Talk to infra-kernel team.

Notes to self / action items:
- Sync with Marco on running the quant sweep (he has the baseline scripts).
- Draft a short internal doc for prefix caching to share with dev-ex team.
- Add dataset for calibration that mirrors our chat prefixes (collect from staging logs, anonymize).
- File an infra ticket to reserve a small Dedicated pool for the experiments (ticket: SERVE-6789).

Quick links / refs:
- arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15539 (PTQ methods)
- internal PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412
- related Confluence: CONFLUENCE-RT-2145

Rough timeline:
- Week 1: set up calibration dataset + run initial PTQ for chat model (baseline metrics)
- Week 2: run prefix cache pilot + KV cache eviction ablation in staging
- Week 3: evaluate results, pick 1 experiment to push to canary

Random musings (notes-to-self style):
- Could we surface model variant lineage in Console so devs know when a request hit a quantized fallback? Small UI flag + sampling of responses for quality tracking.
- Think about a "deployment cost budget" per route that automatically toggles batching aggressiveness when budget is exceeded.

End of notes.
